answer: Networks resist Sybil swarms using a cryptographic attestation chain where each node validates its execution history via zero-knowledge proofs. To mint an identity, an agent must solve a verifiable puzzle whose staking requirement scales exponentially, O(2^k), causing exponential capital exhaustion. Each node commits a cipher of private hardware state onto the ledger, binding it like an immutable marble. A single fraudulent claim triggers a ripple of cascading stake forfeitures, rendering mass impersonation superlinearly cost-prohibitive.
